title: Oxide and Friends 8/5/2024 -- Pragmatic LLM usage with Nicholas Carlini
summary: Nicholas Carlini on pragmatic LLM use: offload tedious, easily verified work, give up quickly when it fails, and judge tools by what they can do.

assertions.quote: I want to do the 10% which is the interesting piece

verdicts.note: Benchmarks and field studies show strong performance on well-specified, common tasks and weaker results on context-heavy, novel logic.

assertions.quote: there's so many things that are easier to verify than write yourself

verdicts.note: Verification cost largely determines whether AI help saves time; field studies find gains concentrate where outputs are cheap to check.

Anthropic: engineers delegate easily verifiable tasks ('amazing for everything where validation effort isn't large in comparison to creation effort'), and time savings came mostly from quickly verifiable tasks.

assertions.quote: you could just keep saying wrong and it will just it will continue to be sorry the whole way through and never fix anything

verdicts.note: Self-correction research shows LLMs rarely fix errors from bare 'that's wrong' feedback, but concrete external feedback such as test output does help iteration.

assertions.quote: if I ask it to write it in rough like just there's not going to be aace Condition

verdicts.note: Compiler checks do catch whole classes of AI errors such as type and data-race bugs, but logic errors still get through and AI does worse in less common languages.

assertions.quote: this might be a case where you more documentation might be even better because if you can give as much help to the model

verdicts.note: Agents parse markdown and commands far more reliably than GUI instructions; llms.txt and markdown docs are spreading for this reason.

assertions.quote: if everyone is relying on these models to use only the things that popular

verdicts.note: Studies show LLMs prefer popular libraries and older APIs, but web search and in-context docs partly offset it, and the effect on adoption is not measured.

assertions.quote: show the model the minimum amount of things so that you're not going to blow the budget

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.

assertions.quote: you can just ask the computer now like the computer's not going to judge you

verdicts.note: Some RCTs (e.g. a Harvard physics AI-tutor study) show learning gains when tutors are scaffolded, but hallucinations and answer-giving can undermine learning.

assertions.quote: I'm hopeful that as they get better they will do this less

verdicts.note: Hallucination rates have fallen markedly in newer models, but they remain non-zero, especially on obscure facts, and are structurally hard to eliminate.

assertions.quote: people should not confuse the coming bust for the the Technologies themselves not being useful

verdicts.note: A market-valuation opinion; not testable from a video's claims.
